newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the retirement of veteran Justin Madden and the loss of Fraser Brown through injury, the Carlton Australian Football League team has moved quickly to rush rookie ruckman Mark Porter into the side for tomorrow's important match against Essendon at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Page 24.

The Australian Rugby League's National Premiership Council, which consists of the 12 ARL clubs, yesterday held further talks with ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker over control of the game. The issue has been the main obstacle to peace in recent talks btween Whittaker and Super League. Page 24.

Canberra Cannons basketball coach Brett Flanigan has pushed veteran centre Ray Borner onto the team's starting line-up and has asked pointguards Brendan Mann and Jamie Pearlman for greater leadership on court as the team prepares for its important match aainst the Melbourne Tigers at Melbourne Park tonight. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian cricketer Ricky Ponting's unbeaten century in the Australian team's match against Glamorgan has boosted his chances of a possible place in the next Test team, and also denied Michael Bevan, who has been batting at No 7, another chance to reaffim his place in the team. Ponting believes his innings will allow him to play in the next match against Middlesex, and it has also helped alleviate the boredom of being unable to bat. Page 43.

South African soccer coach Mich D'Avray, whose team is here on a short tour playing against the Olyroos team, is tipping the Australian soccer team to win an Olympic medal in the Sydney 2000 Games. He says there are so many good players yet to come into what he described as a "very well organised" team. Page 41.

The Sydney Kings basketball team faces up against the Newcastle Falcons tonight, two weeks after suffering a bad loss against them. Sydney's Isaac Burton says that while the team performed well in their win over Brisbane last week, they need to restore some pride and get a win against Newcastle before the NBL competition goes into recess. Page 41.
THE AGE

Athlete Melinda Gainsford-Taylor finished fourth in the 200 metres in Nice on Wednesday, bringing to an end her winning run in Europe. Gainsford-Taylor's coach Jackie Byrnes said the Australian was suffering food poisoning and stomach cramps, and ran an excellent race considering her condition. Page D11.

Australian swimmer Scott Miller may miss the Pan Pacific championships in Japan next month to concentrate on the world championships trials in October. Miller said he has swum in two Pan Pacs, with gold medal success, yet has only competed in one world campionship (Rome, 1994) and did not perform well. Page D11.
THE HERALD SUN

Carlton Australian Football League ruckman Matthew Allan's manager is believed to have received a confidentiality agreement with another AFL club if current negotiations between Allan and Carlton break down. The negotiations have been dogged by disputes over money, and are far from being resolved. Page 108.

A strong debate has surfaced over whether Dean Jones should be appointed as a national selector for the Australian Cricket Board. With 52 Tests and 154 one day internationals, and his first-class captaining experience, he has the credentials, but his outspoken and aggressive style may not suit the ACB. Page 98.

Melbourne Australian Football League ruckman Jimmy Stynes will play his 234th match in a row when the team fronts up against North Melbourne on Sunday, and the game will mark 10 completed seasons since he played in the Melbourne team that defeated Geelong on July 25, 1987. Page 110.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

ACT Brumbies rugby union coach Rod Macqueen will today sign up to stay with the team for another two years. His signing means the team that made it to the final of the Super 12 series against Auckland will be retained, despite large offers from rival clus such as New South Wales. Page 121.

Projected standings of the Australian Football League ladder made at the end of round 15 last weekend - which assume that results from first round clashes will be duplicated - will see Geelong placed on top of the ladder, and the Sydney Swans sneaking in to eighth place. Page 120.

Soccer Australia chairman David Hill said yesterday the Socceroos aimed to be ranked within the top 20 in the world since leaping from 50th to 31st following the appointment of head coach Terry Venables. The Socceroos have won their last 11 appearances uder Venables. Page 121.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
